title: Screwworm and Thanksgiving Travel: What French Bulldog Owners Should Check
seoTitle: Screwworm in Dogs: Thanksgiving Travel Tips
description: Driving to Texas or Arizona with your French Bulldog this Thanksgiving? What USDA and FDA say about New World screwworm in dogs, the daily check and when to call a vet.

faq.q: Can dogs get New World screwworm?
faq.a: Yes. USDA confirmed Arizona's first case in a dog in Cochise County on October 28, 2026, and FDA has authorized emergency treatments for screwworm infestations in dogs.

faq.q: Is my French Bulldog at risk if we travel to Texas or Arizona?
faq.a: FDA says most U.S. dogs are at low risk because cases are in a limited region, but dogs that travel to or return from affected areas should be watched closely. Nothing in the official sources says French Bulldogs are at higher risk than other dogs.

faq.q: What are the signs of screwworm in a dog?
faq.a: Visible maggots or a foul odor in a wound or a body opening such as the eyes, ears, nose or mouth. USDA also asks owners to look for sores around the ears, nose, genital area and navel every day.

faq.q: Can I give Bravecto or NexGard to prevent screwworm?
faq.a: No. The emergency authorizations are for treating an infestation, and Bravecto is prescription-only. Ask your vet before changing any flea and tick product.

faq.q: Where can I check current screwworm cases?
faq.a: USDA APHIS publishes a daily dashboard of confirmed cases in the Current Status section of screwworm.gov. For Texas, the Texas Animal Health Commission lists its infested zones.
